Development Update - Part 1

Undoubtedly, 2022 was an adventure for all of us. We  experienced so many significant accomplishments across multiple facets of our company and community. 2022 was a massive success for us in terms of revenue generation so that we could focus on building out our core team and more. For this update, we will focus on the development of our game specifically so that there is a clear understanding of what is currently being worked on, and what is in store for 2023. First, I'll start off with some context...

Game Loops

Under the hood, game loops are a sequence of programmatic processes (systems) that operate infinitely to deliver an interactive and dynamic experience to the game user. In other words, the primary actions (and the programming associated with those actions) a player takes part in during the game are what defines a game loop, or game loops. On the surface (what the player sees), art and animation will merge with these loops and provide what we call gameplay. Presto!

Game Loop Examples

In my case, when I play Call of Duty and spawn, kill other players, die - then spawn again, is considered a game loop. This loop requires various systems that are continually running in the background that will deliver the gameplay to a player. A very simple example in Cornucopias would be for a player to leave the home bubble in a vehicle, travel to a sector to perform a task, then return to the home bubble. Depending on the game and what the game user decides to do, there is potential for a variety of loops for a player to interact with. As many of you know, Cornucopias will be a massive, open-world game, so you can imagine how many game loops (systems) we will be developing, large and small, to provide a wonderful, immersive, and most of all FUN gaming experience. 

For this update, we will cover some primary systems that are currently in development:

Initial Systems - Early Production
The Initial Game Loop consists of utilizing our desktop launcher to login, open the game, and perform standard pre-game tasks such as customizing your character and choosing gameplay and graphics settings.

@everyone

Art Pipelines - Part 2

Art pipelines are our agile workflow processes that take any visual element of the game from a concept to a game-ready state. This includes but is not limited to all 3d modeling, materials, lighting, animation, and of course large world designing. When art and game loops collide, you have a playable game! 

We have mentioned this before, but it’s worth touching on it again. We, at Cornucopias, decided early on to create our own art from the ground up. This ensures that our art style is 100% unique and of a quality that meets our standards. 

Art pipelines start with an idea which is then submitted for approval. Once approved, the art team will take the idea into a concept and begin production. Something small such as vehicle paint material could demand a few hours of work as to where designing a large world environment can take many months. Each art item will ultimately go through multiple passes before it is considered “game ready”, and this does include performance testing to ensure that the asset will not pose threat to the player's experience.

Every single asset that is brought into Unreal Engine 5 starts in Blender, an open source 3d modeling program. Our 3D artists will model concepts in blender, import those files into UE5, and then apply materials, animations, and programming to make that asset function. Over time, each asset will go through multiple “passes” in which changes and updates will be made until game ready.

Below are some of the tasks at hand in the art department:

Esperanza Sector 1 - Early Production
Esperanza environment is still underway. Foliage, rocks, water and more are being carefully put in place to create an incredible western-themed world.

Mega Dome Pipeline

Calido Valley Raceway - Final Production
This is the Mega Dome that was used for the early testing of our racing game and CNFTCon. Since then, we have made incredible progress. Jim, our technical director has built a custom spline tool that allows our art team to build tracks more efficiently. We are in the final stages of development and are looking forward to releasing early testing to the public in q2 of 2023!

Website, Education Platform, and User Dashboard

Our web team is full steam ahead on building out a very robust and efficient back-end admin for our all new web ecosystem. We are also in early production with the front-end development of our main website which will be launching in early 2023. Once the admin portion of the site is complete, we will move forward with the development of our custom education platform and user dashboard.
